summary: The general half-depth inequality remains open. Exact fixed-memory failures led to a q-step local-inverse dual state. Sublinear q is analytically impossible for the sharp equicorrelation scaling, whereas q proportional to n proves a finite positive constant on that family. A generic conditional-tail Schur lemma and an explicit all-matrix near-identity spectral band were also proved as internal candidates.

claims.statement: For every unit-diagonal SPD B, K(B) is at least (mu/2)B^{-1}, and the corresponding half-depth inequality holds.
assumptions: B is n by n, unit diagonal, and SPD
open_objections: No generic cross-row conditional-tail frame inequality is known
The half-depth statement is stronger than the restricted results proved here

claims.statement: For arbitrary random R_pi, K is bounded below by the optimized deterministic regression certificate P Q^{-1} P^T.
assumptions: All random matrices are square integrable

claims.statement: Neither direct R=D^T nor weighted R=D^T D one-adjacency regression proves the half constant uniformly.

For the q-step local-inverse dual state on rho=c/n positive equicorrelation, q=o(n) fails the half certificate for sufficiently large fixed c, while q/n tending to one half satisfies the limiting half inequality.
open_objections: The limiting result is not a finite-n uniform inequality
It does not cover arbitrary B

claims.statement: Half-linear local-inverse regression proves K(B)>=(25mu/98)B^{-1} for every positive equicorrelation and diagonal-sign conjugate.
assumptions: B is positive equicorrelation or a diagonal-sign conjugate
open_objections: No Lean or other formal certificate exists

claims.statement: Every local-inverse forgotten-history row satisfies r B_O^{-1} r^T <= sigma-mu||d||^2 <=1-mu.
assumptions: d exactly inverts its recent chronological window
open_objections: The rowwise inequality does not control aligned cross-row covariance

claims.statement: If theta=n(1-mu), then K(B)>=[1+theta/sqrt(2)]^{-2}mu B^{-1}; corresponding direct-prefix bounds hold with an additional t/n factor.
assumptions: B is any unit-diagonal SPD matrix
open_objections: The later all-prefix corollary was not separately discussed in the independent audit
